r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: All five REWORK ADDENDUM items reproduced independently. (1) Full clean-env suite at HEAD: 3093 passed, 6 skipped, 1153 subtests, exit 0 -- matches the claim exactly. (2) map/INDEX.md fresh against the committed tree: a rebuild is a zero-byte no-op, and I proved the guard can still fail by mutating the entity count (4743->4742) and watching MapTreeFreshness go red, then restoring byte-identically. (3) All three reworked doc references now assert things that are TRUE of the code, checked by AST not by grep: _rejectionlog() exists and _log_rejection calls it; _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle has zero os.environ/getenv reads and does fall back to __file__; the cited test name exists and .mcp.json's default really is empty. (4) Blast-radius sweep run from the commit itself: 7 identifiers removed, 5 re-bound (moved), 2 genuinely gone, 0 live stranded identifier references at HEAD. (5) The rework changed no behaviour -- the only .py file it touched is AST-identical to 4e1f22cb once docstrings are stripped, with the sources asserted to differ so the probe cannot be vacuous.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: Both g3 commits together (408e6d26..HEAD) touch EXACTLY nine files -- the nine the handoff named, with map/ represented by its only committable artifact map/INDEX.md. The rework commit itself is three: README.md, map/INDEX.md, mcp_spine_server.py. Zero fenced or excluded paths appear: checklist_engine.py, scripts/hooks/**, run_crew.py, gauge_reader.py, install_constellation.py and COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json are all absent from the g3 range. make_demo_spine.py and examples/mcp-interactive-demo/spine.json do appear in the wider a69bbac4..HEAD range but belong to g2, which is closed and excluded from this review. The implementer's one declared departure -- 'points at'->'pointed at' in the same README sentence -- is correct on the merits: .mcp.json's default really is empty, so the present tense was false.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Two of three evidence claims reproduce exactly; the blast-radius claim does not. REPRODUCED: full clean-env suite 3093 passed / 6 skipped / 1153 subtests / exit 0 at HEAD, measured on the committed tree (no tracked modifications outside .agent-work); and the diffstat, 3 files 13+/9-. DOES NOT REPRODUCE: the sweep AFTER count of "0 stranded references in scope". I measure 1 in scope. tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py:201 -- one of the nine files 4e1f22cb changed -- still asserts in its failure message that _spine_open acts on "SPINE_FILE/SPINE_PARENT re-read fresh". Measured against the AST: _spine_open reads SPINE_PARENT from os.environ once (still true) and SPINE_FILE zero times (false, and deliberately so -- removing that read IS the #603 fix). This is the same invalidated claim, in the same words, that the rework fixed at mcp_spine_server.py:962-963. It survived because the sweep grep for the phrase is line-oriented and the message is assembled from two adjacent string literals split as "re-read " + "fresh)", so the phrase appears on no single line. Control: git grep -F for that phrase returns 0 files tree-wide while a whitespace-normalized sweep returns 1 -- the CREW_CONTEXT.md hazard about grepping for a message string. The method hole, not just the instance, is the finding.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Inherited rules hold for this rework. __pycache__ cleared before every measurement I took (#597). No write site is touched at all, so the utf-8/newline rule has no new surface. No trailing whitespace introduced (git diff --check clean). No lint config exists to violate; the README lines land at ~100 cols, matching the paragraph they sit in, and the only very long line is generated map/INDEX.md content. The record-stores-are-never-hand-edited rule holds for map/INDEX.md by measurement, not assertion: a fresh code_map build produces a zero-byte diff, which a hand-edited index would not. The prose itself is an improvement on how-to-talk grounds -- each of the three replacements names the mechanism that actually runs instead of one that was deleted. The one quality-adjacent defect, the line-oriented sweep that could not see a phrase split across two string literals, is recorded against r3-evidence rather than duplicated here.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No divergence that Commander must reconcile inside this gate. The Map Impact claim "no symbol added, removed, renamed or re-signatured" is proven, not accepted: the rework is AST-identical to 4e1f22cb once docstrings are stripped, so the symbol set cannot have moved. Capability claim "none" holds for the same reason. The three decision anchors (one-spine-per-process-stands, fail-closed-beats-fail-open, bind-on-open-over-new-verb) are untouched by this commit. The implementer assumption that the two map/scripts.mcp_spine_server/ pages cannot be committed is TRUE and I verified it at source: .gitignore:73 ignores map/* and un-ignores only INDEX.md and ids.jsonl, so git check-ignore exits 0 on those pages. The handoff request to commit them was impossible, and only map/INDEX.md is a committable map artifact. The generated page on disk did pick up the new docstring. Two out-of-scope divergences flagged as tc1 (an active episode assertion #603 falsified) and tc2 (the fenced spine_rail.py inference, substantive rather than cosmetic). Separately noted and explicitly NOT attributable to this gate: episodes/ carries all eight epic-559 c2 episodes twice, once under active/ with underscore ids and once under retired/ with hyphen ids, bodies differing. No episodes/ file appears anywhere in a69bbac4..HEAD, so this predates the gate entirely.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from <work-id> alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r6-fowler.finding: Pass run over the gate whole change a69bbac4..HEAD, since the rework slice alone is docs and a generated index. 12 smells visited, rail exit 0. FLAGGED 2: feature-envy (_rebind_refusal reaches into the private checklist_engine._active_lease; right trade today, promote at a third caller) and comments-as-deodorant. OVERRIDDEN 5, each with the standard and the reason logged: duplicated-code, data-clumps, primitive-obsession, divergent-change, speculative-generality. ABSENT 5. The pass genuinely moved two verdicts rather than restating my predecessor. shotgun-surgery is absent because this gate CURED it -- the four import-time derivations collapsed into one _telemetry_path, verified by an AST scan finding zero function defaults referencing SPINE/SESSION/ENGINE. comments-as-deodorant stays flagged on a narrower and sharper basis: the three drifted docstrings are genuinely fixed and I checked each against the AST, but one in-scope instance survives at tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py:201, which is the r3 blocker. The data-clumps override is the one worth reading: the obvious Identity value object is exactly the refactoring that would blind the module-wide AST pin guarding this gate core invariant. I also proved the rail can refuse rather than assuming it -- dropping a smell gives REFUSED visit-every-item, blanking an override reason gives REFUSED OVERRIDE-LOG, and the record was restored byte-identically.
